topics.label: Introduction to cancer biology and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, audience, overarching themes, and specific learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Biological foundations: Genetic alterations, tissue architecture, and cell models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer as a stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors: Invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the distinction between benign and malignant neoplasms through their capacity for local invasion and metastasis, their histological progression, and their diagnostic naming conventions.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the specific mechanical, systemic, and metastatic processes through which primary and secondary tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative incidence of tumors across human tissues and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer incidence across different human tissues and across diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles, methods, and limitations of clinical cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological criteria, and practical challenges of screening programs aimed at early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and providing logistical reminders for upcoming practicals.
